index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a methodological pipeline for assessing subject- and group-specific feature importance through repeated randomized trials, designed to stabilize model performance and extract robust feature rankings. The global layout is a horizontal flowchart with six main stages, arranged from left to right: Input Dataset, Model Training (400 Trials), Feature Importance (Per Trial), Top Features (All Trials), Subject-specific Feature Importance, Top Features (All Subjects), and Group-specific Feature Importance. The entire process is structured as a multi-branch workflow, where the input dataset is split into three parallel streams, each representing a separate randomized trial, and all three converge at the final stage.

In the first stage, 'Input Dataset', a stack of three document icons with blue and gray horizontal lines symbolizes the raw data. This feeds into the second stage, 'Model Training (400 Trials)', which is visually represented by three identical branches, each containing a cluster of three interconnected blue cubes (symbolizing a machine learning model) with a small circular icon labeled 'ML' above them, connected by dotted lines to indicate model components or parameters. These three branches are grouped under a large brace labeled 'Repeated Randomized Trials', emphasizing the replication aspect.

Each branch proceeds to the third stage, 'Feature Importance (Per Trial)', depicted as a bar chart with five vertical bars of varying heights and shades of blue, indicating the relative importance of features within a single trial. The next stage, 'Top Features (All Trials)', shows a set of three stylized hand icons, suggesting selection or ranking of top features across all trials within a single subject’s data stream.

This leads to the fifth stage, 'Subject-specific Feature Importance', illustrated by a bar chart similar to the previous one but now with a glowing lightbulb icon above it, symbolizing insight or derived importance specific to an individual subject. The three subject-specific outputs then converge into the sixth stage, 'Top Features (All Subjects)', again represented by three hand icons, indicating aggregation of top features across all subjects.

Finally, the seventh stage, 'Group-specific Feature Importance', displays a bar chart with five bars of increasing height and color intensity from light to dark blue, representing the consolidated, group-level feature importance derived from the aggregated subject-level results. All connections between stages are shown as solid blue arrows, indicating the direction of data flow. The visual design uses consistent blue tones for data and model elements, with black text for labels and titles, ensuring clarity and focus on the methodological progression.
